title: Investigate and remediate rate-limit fanout causing per-model chart shadowing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Symptoms: several customer-facing Console charts (per-model hourly breakdowns and the top-models widget) have shown a persistent suppression of short-lived spikes after a nightly backfill window. Spikes are present in raw event logs but are flattened or moved across neighboring hours in the dashboard. This leads to under-estimated peak token usage for some customers and confusing billing / quota narratives.

Initial hypothesis: a rate-limit enforcement path in the ingest tier performs a fanout to multiple shard replicas for headroom accounting. When the ingestion watermark/backfill runner replays delayed events, the fanout path emitted duplicate tokens with different transient ids. Downstream deduplication relies on a per-event id that the backfill path does not preserve, so duplicates survive into the aggregation window. The console smoothing algorithm then applies an outlier-suppression pass to protect charts from single-hour spikes, and because the duplicates are spread across adjacent hour buckets the suppression algorithm reduces the visible spike, producing the observed flattened trend.

Why this is bad: customers see inaccurate peak hours and per-model top-k lists, capacity teams cannot trust spike reports for scaling decisions, and billing reconciliations for quota enforcement become noisy. We need a fix that preserves correct accounting while remaining performant and backwards-compatible for historical backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Backfills that re-ingest the same logical request must not create duplicate token counts in the hourly aggregator (no >0.1% divergence from raw canonical ledger after fix)
Per-model top-k and hourly peak charts reflect the same totals as reconciled ledger within margin of error for at least three customers previously impacted
No material regression (<2% P95 latency increase) in the ingest hot path during normal traffic
Rollout plan validated: can be toggled by feature flag and safely rolled back without data loss
reproduction_steps: 1) Use replay harness against staging: take a night's worth of streaming rate-limited events and replay them through the backfill runner with slight timestamp jitter (±2 minutes).
2) Enable ingest rate-limit fanout path in staging and compare aggregator counts with and without fanout dedup disabled.
3) Run console smoothing pipeline and observe per-model hourly charts rendered via the staging console. Expect flattened spikes if dedup fails.
4) Query raw ledger rows by request_id and token_hash to confirm duplicates are present in the aggregator input but absent in canonical upstream source.
proposed_solution: Short-term (surgical): add an idempotency key to fanout replicas derived from stable request identifiers (canonical request_id + origin) so backfill and live paths generate identical dedupe keys.
Medium-term: extend aggregator dedup window to consider stable idempotency keys and token_hash pairs when merging shard inputs for a given hour.

Long-term: remove smoothing algorithm sensitivity to low-cardinality duplicates by switching from outlier-suppression heuristic to a tested, statistically robust spike detector that references raw ledger reconciliations for verification before muting a spike.

Operational: provide a retroactive reconciliation job that consumes the canonical ledger and emits correction deltas for affected hourly buckets; surface these corrections in the console UI as ‘reconciled adjustments’ so customers understand changes.
implementation_notes: - Touch points: ingest-service (fanout), backfill-runner, shard-merge aggregator, console-timeseries pipeline, smoothing library.
- Backwards compatibility: the new idempotency key must be optional and accepted by older aggregator nodes to avoid split-brain during rollout. Use feature-flag gating keyed to release channels.
- Data migration: reconciliation job will emit synthetic correction events; mark them with origin=reconcile to keep them distinguishable from normal events.
- Performance: adding idempotency key computation is cheap (stable hash of request_id + origin). Dedup window expansion needs benchmarking against peak traffic (target <5% CPU for aggregator shard).
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy idempotency-key generation to ingest-service behind FF
2) Deploy aggregator change to respect idempotency key in dedup logic to a canary pool (10% of shards)
3) Run replay tests and internal reconciliations for canary customers for 24h
4) If stable, expand to 50% then 100%
5) Enable reconciliation job and surface reconciled deltas in Console with a footer note
6) Switch smoothing algorithm on a separate FF after 2 weeks of stable aggregates
testing_notes: Unit tests for idempotency key creation and equality semantics
Integration tests: staged backfill replay with and without dedup and asserted aggregator totals
Load test: simulate peak traffic with fanout enabled and monitor aggregator CPU and ingestion latency
E2E: Console chart snapshot tests for previously failing customer accounts (links below)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: aggregator dedup expansion could increase memory footprint per-hour window. Mitigation: implement a bounded LRU with rare-eviction counters and fall back to reconciler for any ambiguous buckets.

Risk: reconciliation job may create visible corrections that alarm customers. Mitigation: include human-readable explanation and prior-notice in release notes; limit surface to accounts with >1% delta.

Risk: rolling change could create temporary discrepancy between Console and billing. Mitigation: coordinate with Billing team and put a short hold on automated invoices for impacted customers during rollout window.
